answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents map interactions onto an identity atlas where topological cut verifications detect sparse graph bottlenecks. Randomly assigned auditor cliques cross-examine transaction flows, placing a high-stake bond on a verification ledge. If a multi-agent audit catches coordinated fraudulent claims, stake slashing triggers immediately. Such interdependent edge cuts and verification games force an attacker to incur superlinear cost scaling with fraud size, making a yarrow bloom of fake identities economically unviable.
